Every Writer path shares a pre-Store generation-admission decision; current plus at most 64 retired generations, with explicit known-not-committed backpressure at retire, incremental-merge capacity, or paired lane slot/byte exhaustion. The immutable base uses an exact 64-byte record plus 5 bytes of lookup payload per bucket; a sequence-coherent per-lane census exposes the current generation's allocation-payload lower bound without presenting it as total RSS. Large immutable-record arrays use guarded geometric mappings with at most one spare per base lineage; the spare-pool lock is absent from GET and ordinary Delta publication and process-wide spare bytes are observable. Incremental merge debt is advanced proportionally to the bounded post-cut capacity consumed by the next publication, with a bounded coalesced-batch floor and explicit debt, capacity, and maximum-quantum telemetry; fixed terminal retry bursts are not the normal admission mechanism.

data.descrizione: memory_reserve_bytes bounds the RAM a durable Store keeps for derived state. data.descrizione: Durable Stores serve GETs of resident Segments from in-memory images admitted under the Store memory reserve (ADR 0045 as amended by ADR 0046). The Writer mirrors each Record into the active image before the append and publication; compaction outputs are mirrored while staged; images are loaded at open within the reserve. A resident read applies the cold path's CRC32C, identity, key/hash and expiry validation without a file read, and completes on the calling thread (embedded caller or glifistored Reader) without a disk-read lane when the Record fits the caller's response budget. Segments without an image keep the pinned cold path. In glifistored a connection keeps up to 32 GET responses in ordered slots behind its oldest cold read, reserved against the output watermark and released in request order. Acknowledgement, visibility, recovery authority, persistence v1 and wire v2 are unchanged.

data.descrizione: Benchmark CI emits median ops/s deltas against the previous baseline only when the recorded environment and benchmark-contract identities match, including each result's operation, warmup, and repeat counts. Hosted results and the 10% review threshold are advisory regression signals; overlapping min/max ranges remain inconclusive, not a hard release gate or absolute product claim. Retained CI reports fail closed on incomplete or internally inconsistent benchmark output and on sampling weaker than the fixed source contract. Same-revision deltas are preserved as repeat-variance evidence and cannot be classified as code regression or improvement candidates. Hosted runs also bind comparisons to recorded CMake and Ninja identities and retain a versioned digest of the invocation workflow plus tracked build, product, and benchmark-source inputs. Identical benchmark subjects across different commits are classified as repeat variance because the measured code/configuration is unchanged; missing or changed subjects do not hide candidates. Complete TCP matrices validate filename/runtime coordinates and derive per-depth Worker speedup, scaling efficiency, and the highest observed median pipeline. The hosted contract also requires ordered Reactor input/output-buffer compaction and copied-byte profiles, normalized per timed operation in the report. It derives the smallest measured pipeline retaining at least 95% of the best same-Worker median, exposing that economical depth as advice rather than silently changing client behavior. Same-process TCP samples record their client/Reactor/Writer foreground-thread floor, while the retained environment records logical and physical CPU counts. The report labels rows exceeding either capacity as oversubscription sensitivity measurements rather than physical-core scaling evidence. Durable profile summaries require explicit durable storage metadata and cannot be inferred from shared completion counters alone. First-party specialized CSV/TSV benchmarks emit the common evidence metadata and are parsed into direction-aware structured diagnostics with complete repeat identities and ordered ranges; these diagnostics remain advisory unless a separate reviewed budget explicitly promotes them into a gate.

cause: Cold live data at the head of the sealed history must be copied before newer dead space is reachable (prefix head-of-line; range compaction deferred by ADR 0044)
Foreground PUT/ERASE on the compacted Worker are rejected while the commit gate is armed
O(N) Phase A Index enumeration under synchronization for very large Workers
At emergency, peak-budget planning (current Segments + outputs) exceeds max_store_bytes when max_store_bytes leaves less than one compaction output of headroom over max_segment_count
conseguenze: Reclaim lags the write rate when cold live prefixes dominate, and Segment count grows
Emergency rejects mutations while compaction is refused for the peak budget (manual repair)
Foreground PUT/ERASE on the compacted Worker fail with sequence_conflict while the gate is held
contenimento: Pressure and emergency bypass pacing and the per-cycle copy cap; emergency stops new writes
Remap, superseded copies, rebases, Manifest conflicts and abandoned bytes are counted (remapped_records, superseded_copies, manifest_rebases, manifest_conflict_aborts, abandoned_copy_bytes)
data.evento_pericoloso: Background compaction cannot keep up and the durable Store stops accepting writes
prevenzione: ADR 0044 commit-time remap removes the journal limit; rebase removes rotation aborts; prefix selection bounds each transaction by max_copy_bytes_per_cycle instead of skipping the Worker
Keep max_store_bytes >= max_segment_count Segments + max_temporary_compaction_bytes
data.rischio_residuo: Exploratory local measurement on 2026-11-14 (macOS arm64, Debug library, harness not retained): 1 Worker, 128 MiB live, 4 KiB random overwrites, 128 MiB/s pacing, no per-cycle cap. At about 6,000 op/s ADR 0044 completed 8 of 12 attempts in 25 s with zero abandoned copy bytes and 4 to 5 Segments (ADR 0043 baseline 2026-11-13: 0 of 39, about 1 GiB abandoned, 17 Segments); 0.19% of PUTs returned sequence_conflict at the commit gate. At about 12,500 op/s it completed 10 of 16 with 4 to 6 Segments and 1.2% sequence_conflict. Not a retained campaign: no tail-latency, multi-Worker, Linux/BSD or Release evidence. The emergency capacity wedge with max_store_bytes equal to max_segment_count + 1 Segments is unchanged.

data.accettazione_rischio: Architectural prototype only; no release acceptance
cause: Image unmapped while a Reader still holds a generation that references it
Publication of a Record reference before its image bytes are written
Media corruption after load is not observed because resident reads skip the file
conseguenze: Use-after-free or wrong value returned to the client
Silent divergence between served value and on-disk Record until eviction, compaction or restart
contenimento: Cold path keeps full validation and fails closed
Recovery, compaction and backup verification re-validate persisted Records
resident_reads_enabled=false restores file reads for every Segment
data.evento_pericoloso: A durable GET returns bytes that no longer match the persisted Record, or reads a released image
prevenzione: An image is owned by the generations that share it and unmapped only when the last one is reclaimed
The Writer mirrors bytes before the append, so publication of the reference follows them
Resident reads verify CRC32C, identity, key/hash and expiry exactly as cold reads
data.rischio_residuo: Implemented locally (ADR 0046). The resident-read test demonstrates that post-load media damage is served from the image; the cold-path test with images disabled proves detection. Eviction concurrent with Readers has not yet run under TSan.

data.accettazione_rischio: Architectural prototype only; no release acceptance
cause: The spill directory's filesystem is full when a page is first written
Copy-on-write filesystems need new blocks on every page write
A snapshot or clone shares the spill file's blocks, so a page write needs new ones
conseguenze: SIGBUS during an Index update; the process stops and restart recovers from the log
contenimento: The Index is derived state; restart rebuilds it from the log (ADR 0004)
Operators can place the spill directory on a dedicated filesystem
data.evento_pericoloso: An Index spill-file page fault terminates the process
prevenzione: Spill is opt-in through index_spill_directory; the default pages anonymously to swap
Every platform reserves the spill file's blocks before mapping it (F_PREALLOCATE on macOS, posix_fallocate on Linux and FreeBSD, zero writes on OpenBSD or when the filesystem refuses)
A spill file whose blocks cannot be reserved is never mapped; the array stays in anonymous memory
macOS retries a failed contiguous reservation without contiguity, including ENOSPC due to fragmentation
The spill file is unlinked at creation and never synchronized, so nothing survives a crash
data.rischio_residuo: Copy-on-write filesystems (and snapshots sharing the file) may still allocate on a page write and raise SIGBUS when full. The fallback is proven locally on macOS with a file-size limit and a fault-injected reservation failure; no platform-row CI evidence yet.

data.accettazione_rischio: Architectural prototype only; no release acceptance
cause: A sibling rejected before it touches the pending group (erase of an absent key, exhausted live-key budget, validation or admission limit) is treated like a failure of the append attempt
Any client can send such a request behind unflushed siblings of the same Writer group
conseguenze: Earlier siblings that were committed in memory are reported unavailable or INTERNAL_ERROR although the rejection is unrelated to them
Every later mutation is rejected until the Store or daemon restarts, so one benign request removes write availability for all clients
contenimento: A failure during or after the append attempt still abandons the unflushed prefix fail-closed
Recovery after a fail-closed stop is unchanged
data.evento_pericoloso: A routine rejected request fails the whole durable runtime closed in durable_group mode
prevenzione: The runtime marks a rejection as rejected_before_append only at returns that precede the append attempt; the Writer batch keeps the unflushed prefix and commits it with the sub-batch (ADR 0047)
A result without that mark keeps the fail-closed default
data.rischio_residuo: Implemented locally (ADR 0047, accepted). The tests place one rejected sibling behind a successful one on the batch API and on the daemon's asynchronous lane; they ran under ASan, UBSan and TSan on macOS arm64 without reports. There is no mixed-workload soak. Known-not-committed results outside the class (append, rotation, flush, exception paths) keep abandoning the prefix, so a before-hook failure at append, or a compaction Index-gate conflict, behind an unflushed sibling still fails the runtime closed.

data.accettazione_rischio: Not accepted for release; fixed-owner capacity limit remains unresolved
cause: Fixed key ownership and no runtime load redistribution (ADR 0033)
A hot key or asymmetric request distribution concentrates work on one Reader or Writer
conseguenze: Throughput is limited by the hot shard rather than aggregate CPU capacity
Tail latency and bounded-lane backpressure increase for traffic targeting that owner
contenimento: Bounded lanes constrain queued work but do not redistribute it
data.evento_pericoloso: A hot shard saturates while other shard pairs retain unused capacity
prevenzione: No dynamic balancing mechanism is implemented; a solution remains to be studied
ADR 0048 removes intermediate materialization of small volatile GET values within the Reader lease
data.rischio_residuo: Open capacity limitation. The retained local Release exploration on 2026-11-21 compares 75 and 90 percent finite total-work allocations with balanced client bindings. It validates the measurement tooling, not sustained offered-load saturation or sibling isolation: cold clients can finish early. Ten-client rows have a 14-thread foreground floor on 10 logical CPUs and remain oversubscription sensitivity observations. Single-hot-key contention, per-owner CPU/queue decomposition, long overlap and native Linux/BSD campaigns are pending. A shard pair is not a single CPU core. Offline migration is not runtime balancing and does not by itself resolve a single hot key. ADR 0048's local old/candidate/old comparison shows a reduction in Reader copy work (about 9 percent for the hot-owner 1 KiB GET case), not runtime redistribution or a general tail-latency improvement. Compaction sustainability remains separate.

data.accettazione_rischio: Not accepted for release; problem recorded only, solution deferred
cause: INIT is followed by one BIND_WORKER binding the connection to one owner
A request key belongs to a different owner from the bound connection
conseguenze: The server returns WRONG_OWNER instead of executing or forwarding the request
Clients must manage owner-specific routing and connections; mismatch can interrupt application work
contenimento: Wrong-owner requests are rejected rather than applied to the wrong shard
Official clients mark the client unhealthy under client-semantics-v1
data.evento_pericoloso: Client routing mismatch rejects requests without server-side forwarding
prevenzione: Clients use the routing identity and owner metadata defined by wire v2
data.rischio_residuo: Open integration limitation of the current routing contract, not a claim that WRONG_OWNER violates wire v2. Connection management and recovery remain client responsibilities. The availability and connection-cost impact needs measurement; no transparent forwarding, automatic reroute or retry guarantee is introduced. A solution remains to be studied separately from online rebalancing.
